outcome: clinical presentation of tubal ectopic pregnancies
cohort: The study included 76 cases of tubal ectopic pregnancies at a tertiary center, divided into pre-pandemic (January 2018 to February 2020) and pandemic (March 2020 to February 2022) groups.
finding: The study found no statistically significant differences in the clinical presentation, treatment management, hospitalization duration, blood transfusion needs, or incidence of ruptured ectopic pregnancies between the pre-pandemic and pandemic groups.
